items.title: Total Annihilation, rebuilt for modern computers
items.summary: The classic game Total Annihilation has been successfully rebuilt to run on modern computers, enhancing its accessibility for a new generation of players. This development is significant for game developers interested in retro gaming and preservation techniques.

items.title: NYC's 'Click to Cancel' rule is now in effect
items.summary: New regulations in New York City require businesses to implement a 'Click to Cancel' feature for subscriptions, enhancing consumer rights and transparency. This change is crucial for web developers to understand as it impacts how subscription services are designed and managed.

items.title: LineageOS 24.0
items.summary: The latest version of LineageOS, a popular open-source Android operating system, has been released, featuring numerous updates and improvements. This is important for developers in the mobile space who are interested in custom ROM development and Android system modifications.

items.title: Valen's Memory Safety: A New Kind of Borrow Checking
items.summary: Valen introduces a novel approach to memory safety with a new kind of borrow checking that aims to enhance programming language safety features. This development is essential for systems programmers and language designers focused on improving memory management.

items.title: I paid people to try and follow my README
items.summary: A developer shares insights from an experiment where they paid users to follow their README documentation, revealing critical usability issues. This story is valuable for open-source contributors and maintainers looking to improve documentation and user experience.
